subject: Physics
exam_context: JEE Main 2026 (Paper 1, B.E./B.Tech) — Physics section only, 25 questions/100 marks
data_provenance: Estimated from PYQ-trend analysis and chapter-wise-weightage trackers aggregated across the 2025 and 2026 (Jan + Apr) sessions (not official NTA data); last grounded Sep 2026. Individual-session weightage varies shift to shift; treat these as multi-session averages for question-bank planning, not a guarantee of any single paper's composition.

M01.notes: Short, scoring unit when it appears; rarely more than 1 question per session.

M02.notes: Often fused with Laws of Motion in a single question; foundational rather than a big standalone scorer.

M03.notes: Friction and constraint-based problems recur across sessions.

M04.notes: Collision numericals are a recurring, formula-driven favourite.

M05.notes: One of the highest-weightage Mechanics chapters; rolling/moment-of-inertia numericals recur every session.

M06.notes: Escape velocity and orbital energy numericals are the most common archetype.

M07.notes: Fluid mechanics (Bernoulli, viscosity, surface tension) supplies most of this unit's questions.

M08.notes: Consistently flagged as a top-priority chapter across trackers; first-law and specific-heat numericals dominate.

M09.notes: Usually tested via rms-speed / degrees-of-freedom numericals, often paired conceptually with Thermodynamics.

M10.notes: A broad, combined unit (SHM + wave motion + sound); questions are usually single-concept given the removal of damped/forced-oscillation and Doppler sub-topics.

M11.notes: Combines electrostatics and capacitance in one unit for JEE Main; consistently a top-3 weighted Physics unit.

M12.notes: Repeatedly the single highest-weightage Physics chapter in session-wise trackers (Wheatstone bridge, potentiometer, Kirchhoff's-law numericals).

M13.chapter: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
M13.notes: Biot-Savart/Ampere's-law numericals and moving-coil-galvanometer conversions recur often.

M14.notes: LCR resonance and EMI numericals are a recurring high-weightage archetype.

M15.notes: Mostly conceptual/recall (spectrum identification, E/B/c relations); rarely more than one question.

M16.notes: Combines Ray Optics and Wave Optics in one unit for JEE Main; flagged as a top chapter across multiple 2026 trackers.

M17.chapter: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
M17.notes: Photoelectric-effect stopping-potential numericals are the dominant archetype.

M18.notes: Bohr-model transitions and radioactive-decay numericals recur; together with M17 this makes 'Modern Physics' one of the highest-weightage groupings.

M19.notes: Not tested in JEE Advanced at all. Diode I-V characteristics and logic-gate truth tables are direct, NCERT-diagram-based questions with a rising weightage trend in recent sessions.

M20.notes: A dedicated syllabus unit unique to JEE Main (JEE Advanced tests experiments as part of its Units/Errors topic instead, not as a separate weighted unit). Several trackers describe this as a highly predictable, pattern-based source of easy marks.

broad_category_weightage_pct.note: Coarser cross-check figures, approximate % share of the 25-question Physics section, synthesised from multiple 2025-2026 PYQ trend sources. Rounds do not sum to exactly 100% because a few marginal units (EM Waves, Experimental Skills overlap) are reported inconsistently across sources.
broad_category_weightage_pct.Experimental_Skills (M20): 5-8% (one source claims as high as 20%; treated here with caution as an outlier estimate)

marking_scheme.source_note: Confirmed via multiple Sep 2026 sources reporting on the actual Jan 2026 and Apr 2026 JEE Main sessions.
marking_scheme.section_a_mcq: 20 single-correct MCQs per subject; +4 for a correct answer, -1 for an incorrect answer, 0 if unattempted.
marking_scheme.section_b_numerical: 5 numerical-value questions per subject, all compulsory (the earlier 'attempt any 5 of 10' choice was removed starting with the 2025 pattern); +4 for a correct answer, -1 for an incorrect answer, 0 if unattempted. This differs from pre-2025 sessions, when numerical questions carried no negative marking.
marking_scheme.question_types_used: Single-correct MCQ and numerical-value only. JEE Main does NOT use multiple-correct MCQs or matrix-match questions — those formats are exclusive to JEE Advanced.
